result.title: Amortized Thompson Sampling and Efficient Information-Directed Sampling for Simulator-Based Design
result.summary: Thompson sampling is a widely used strategy for sequential decision-making under uncertainty, offering a principled way to balance exploration and exploitation. This strategy involves maximizing a target objective under a single sample drawn from the current belief over unknown quantities. Conventionally, this optimization is performed once the belief has been inferred from data, and it becomes computationally burdensome when many Thompson samples are required, especially in continuous action spaces. In this work, we introduce an approach that amortizes this process ahead of time, before any data is collected, so that an approximation of the full Thompson sampling distribution is available immediately once observations arrive. We employ this approach to solve the multi-round setting, involving sequential data acquisition and Thompson-sample recommendation across rounds. Beyond accelerating Thompson sampling, our approach enables efficient estimation of expected information gain about the optimal action. This can be used to select more informative Thompson samples or to obtain maximally informative designs with optimization. Combining this estimate of expected information gain with immediate regret supports information-directed sampling (IDS), which can outperform Thompson sampling by explicitly balancing these two quantities. We demonstrate our approach on two simulator-based design problems in synthetic biology, where the simulators have intractable likelihoods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出在收集任何数据之前就预先摊销 Thompson sampling，使观测到达后能立即得到完整采样分布的近似；并借此高效估计关于最优动作的期望信息增益，支撑多轮序列设计与 information-directed sampling，在似然不可解的两个合成生物学模拟器设计问题上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信念状态→摊销采样→信息增益→采集决策」的链条可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与 LOOK/STOP 的价值估计提供概念线索，但属较远领域，迁移性有待核查。
